summary: This work presents a systematic evaluation of deep learning architectures for mitigating noise in quantum circuit output probability distributions using IBM 5-qubit superconducting processors and over 246,000 unique circuits. Attention-based models, particularly the Transformer and Perceiver, consistently outperform classical baselines (SPAM, Repolarizer, Mix, Thresholding) and simpler neural networks, achieving mitigation on ~80% of real hardware circuits by reducing the $L_1$ distance between noisy and ideal distributions.
motivation: Quantum error mitigation requires exponentially more samples using standard methods, motivating investigation of machine learning approaches that can learn noise patterns from data-driven supervision to improve practical utility of near-term quantum devices.
method: Models ranging from MLPs to sequence-to-sequence attention architectures were trained on 8,000 simulated circuits per depth value, fine-tuned on real data from ibm_algiers (5-qubit subset, 15,000 circuits per depth, January–April 2024), and evaluated via ablation studies, cross-dataset generalization, and transfer to ibm_hanoi using KL-divergence loss with pre-training and 50-trial Bayesian hyperparameter optimization.
result: The Perceiver achieved median $L_1$ Relative Change of $-0.2062$ (83.2% circuits improved) on real Pauli data and $-0.0210$ (64.4% improved) on real Random data; transfer to ibm_hanoi without retraining showed comparable performance; ablations revealed the noisy distribution is the dominant input feature, circuit information weakly exploited, and attention mechanisms most robust to distribution shift across circuit types and devices.
